provenance.orgName: Hyde (Hida, formerly New Minster, Winchester), Hampshire. Benedictine abbey of Holy Trinity, St Mary the Virgin, and St Peter
provenance.p: This attribution was first added in the Medieval Libraries of Great Britain Supplement (1987), having been transferred here from Winchester (St Swithun). The corresponding Medieval Libraries of Great Britain index card records the following information: Ed. D. H. Turner, The Missal of the New Minster, Winchester, Henry Bradshaw Society 93 (1962); reduced facsimile of fol. 62r, see pp. viii-xiiii. Turner says Stowe 2 and Le Havre 330 seem to have a scribe or scribes in common.

provenance.orgName: Winchester, Hampshire, Benedictine cathedral priory of St Peter, St Paul, and St Swithun (Old Minster)
provenance.p: This attribution was accepted in the second edition of Medieval Libraries of Great Britain (1964). However, in the Supplement (1987), the attribution was rejected in favour of Hyde. The corresponding Medieval Libraries of Great Britain index card for Winchester (St Swithun) originally cited the following older literature, which was later deemed unsatisfactory for an attribution: Cf. L. Delisle and C. Fierville in Rev. des sociétés savantes, 7eme série, 6 (1882) p. 33, with facsimiles; Mémoires de la Soc. havraise d'études diverses (1880–1881), pp. 401–546, and V. Leroquais, Les sacramentaires et les Milssels, 1. 190. Liturgy points to Winchester (St Swithun) or Hyde.

recordHist.source: Neil R. Ker, ed., Medieval Libraries of Great Britain: A List of Surviving Books, Royal Historical Society Guides and Handbooks, 3 (London, 1941; 2nd edn, 1964; supplement, ed. Andrew G. Watson, 1987; digital edn, ed. Richard Sharpe and James M. W. Willoughby, 2010–15).
